input: To what team was the 2014 NBA Rookie of the Year traded in October 2016?
expected_output: Michael Carter-Williams, the 2014 NBA Rookie of the Year, was traded to the Chicago Bulls in October 2016.
context: The 2016–17 Chicago Bulls season was the 51st season of the franchise in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Former 2011 MVP and 2009 Rookie of the Year Derrick Rose was traded from his hometown team to the New York Knicks. This was the first season without Rose since the 2012–13 season. Dwyane Wade, who played for the Miami Heat from 2003 to 2016, decided to leave the Heat and sign with his hometown team, the Chicago Bulls. The Bulls traded Tony Snell to the Milwaukee Bucks for Michael Carter-Williams on October 17, 2016.

Michael Carter-Williams (born October 10, 1991) is an American professional basketball player for the Charlotte Hornets of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He was drafted 11th overall in the 2013 NBA draft by the Philadelphia 76ers, after playing college basketball for the Syracuse Orange. He was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2014, and has also played for the Milwaukee Bucks and Chicago Bulls.

The Milwaukee Bucks entered the 2016–17 season looking to build around a young core after trading away veteran guard Michael Carter-Williams, who had struggled with injuries during his tenure with the team following his acquisition from the Philadelphia 76ers in 2015.

Ernest DiGregorio, known as "Ernie D." (born January 15, 1951), is an American former National Basketball Association player. He was the 1973–74 NBA Rookie of the Year and holds the NBA rookie record for assists in a single game with 25. Due to a severe knee injury suffered early in DiGregorio's professional career, he played only five NBA seasons.

Tyreke Jamir Evans (born September 19, 1989) is an American professional basketball player for the Memphis Grizzlies of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He played college basketball at the University of Memphis and was selected by the Kings with the 4th overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft. Evans was the 2010 NBA Rookie of the Year winner and was traded to the New Orleans Pelicans in 2013, before being traded back to the Kings in 2017.

The Tour de France is an annual men's multiple stage bicycle race primarily held in France, while also occasionally passing through nearby countries. The race was first organized in 1903 to increase sales for the newspaper L'Auto, and is currently run by the Amaury Sport Organisation.

input: Bob Edwards was the host of what show, that later was hosted by Renee Montagne?
expected_output: Bob Edwards was the host of "Morning Edition," which was later hosted by Renee Montagne.
context: Robert Alan "Bob" Edwards (born May 16, 1947) is an American broadcast journalist, a Peabody Award-winning member of the National Radio Hall of Fame. He gained reputation as the first host of National Public Radio's flagship program, "Morning Edition". Starting in 2004, Edwards then was the host of "The Bob Edwards Show" on Sirius XM Radio.

Renée Montagne is an American radio journalist and was the co-host (with Steve Inskeep and David Greene) of National Public Radio's weekday morning news program, "Morning Edition", from May 2004 to November 11, 2016. Montagne and Inskeep succeeded longtime host Bob Edwards, initially as interim replacements.

The Bob Edwards Show is an American radio program previously presented by Sirius XM Satellite Radio every weekday morning at 8 a.m. Eastern. The program was heard on the Sirius XM Public Radio station at XM channel 121 and Sirius channel 205.

On June 23, 2015, NPR's Renee Montagne reported on Morning Edition that academics, librarians and history students had been rallying around the hashtag Charleston Syllabus, suggesting readings that might help inform the public of the city's racial history.

input: Who was Chamberlain and Colonel of the military staff of The Merrie Monarch?
expected_output: Colonel Charles Hastings Judd was Chamberlain and Colonel of the military staff of The Merrie Monarch.
context: Colonel Charles Hastings Judd (September 8, 1835 – April 18, 1890) was an American businessman, rancher, courtier and politician of the Kingdom of Hawaii. He served as Chamberlain and Colonel of the military staff of King Kalākaua and traveled with the monarch on his 1881 world tour.

Kalākaua (November 16, 1836 – January 20, 1891), born David Laʻ amea Kamananakapu Mahinulani Naloiaehuokalani Lumialani Kalākaua and sometimes called The Merrie Monarch, was the last king (and second to last monarch) of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻ i, reigning from 1874 until his death in 1891.

The muumuu is a loose dress of Hawaiian origin that hangs from the shoulder. Muumuus continue to be the preferred formal dress for weddings and festivals such as the Merrie Monarch hula competition, which is named in honor of King Kalākaua.

input: Which came first, Battle of Antietam or Battle of Guam?
expected_output: The Battle of Antietam came first, occurring on September 17, 1862, while the First Battle of Guam took place from 8 December to 10 December 1941.
context: The Battle of Antietam, also known as the Battle of Sharpsburg, was fought on September 17, 1862, near Sharpsburg, Maryland and Antietam Creek as part of the Maryland Campaign. It was the first field army-level engagement in the Eastern Theater of the American Civil War to take place on Union soil and is the bloodiest single-day battle in American history.

The First Battle of Guam was an engagement during the Pacific War in World War II, and took place from 8 December to 10 December 1941 on Guam in the Mariana Islands between Japan and the United States. The American garrison was defeated by Japanese forces on 10 December.

The Second Battle of Guam (21 July – 10 August 1944) was the American recapture of the Japanese-held island of Guam, a U.S. territory in the Mariana Islands captured by the Japanese from the U.S. in the 1941 First Battle of Guam.

William Farrar Smith, known as 'Baldy' Smith, was a Union general in the American Civil War, notable for attracting the extremes of glory and blame. He was praised for his gallantry in the Seven Days Battles and the Battle of Antietam, but was demoted for insubordination after the disastrous defeat at Fredericksburg.
The Battle of Midway was a major naval battle in the Pacific Theater of World War II, fought between the United States and Japan in June 1942, roughly six months after the Guam engagements.

input: Which English musician is known for both the songs "See Yourself" and "Withing You Without You"?
expected_output: George Harrison is the English musician known for both the songs "See Yourself" and "Within You Without You".
context: "See Yourself" is a song by English musician George Harrison, released on his 1976 album "Thirty Three & 1/3". Harrison began writing the song in 1967, while he was a member of the Beatles, in response to the public outcry surrounding Paul McCartney's admission that he had taken LSD.

"Within You Without You" is a song written by George Harrison and released on the Beatles' 1967 album "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band". It was Harrison's second composition in the Indian classical style, after "Love You To", inspired by his stay in India with Ravi Shankar.

English musician Syd Barrett recorded many songs during his short career as a founding member of Pink Floyd, writing most of the material on their first album, "The Piper at the Gates of Dawn", before leaving the music business entirely in 1972.

No Plan is an extended play comprising songs written and recorded by English musician David Bowie, released posthumously on 8 January 2017, compiling songs written for Bowie's Broadway musical "Lazarus".

input: Alexander S. Wadsworth served during the war that was faught between which two countries?
expected_output: The War of 1812 was fought between the United States and the United Kingdom. Alexander S. Wadsworth served during this war.
context: Commodore Alexander Scammel Wadsworth (1790–April 5, 1851) was an officer of the United States Navy. His more than 40 years of active duty included service in the War of 1812.

The War of 1812 (1812–1815) was a conflict fought between the United States, the United Kingdom, and their respective allies. Historians in Britain often see it as a minor theater of the Napoleonic Wars; in the United States and Canada, it is seen as a war in its own right.

Elisha Strong Wadsworth (May 10, 1813 – November 25, 1890) was a merchant from New Hartford, Connecticut, who co-founded the Wadsworth, Dyer & Chapin company in Chicago, Illinois, trading in dry goods, grain, and packaged meat.

Bilateral relations between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the United States began in 1933 when full diplomatic relations were established, and the two countries have since been described as having a 'Special Relationship'.

input: Are both Dafeng District and Dazhou located in the same province?
expected_output: No, Dafeng District is located in Jiangsu province, while Dazhou is located in Sichuan province.
context: Dafeng () is a coastal district under the administration of Yancheng, Jiangsu province, China. Located on the Jiangsu North Plain with a coastline of 112 km, Dafeng was historically one of the largest salt-making areas in China and now is famed for its well preserved eco-system.
Dazhou () is a prefecture-level city in the northeast corner of Sichuan province, China, bordering Shaanxi to the north and Chongqing to the east and south. 2002 population was 384,525.
Yandu District () is one of three districts of Yancheng, Jiangsu province, China. (The other two are Tinghu District and Dafeng District).
Sichuan–Shanghai gas pipeline is a 1702 km long natural gas pipeline in China. The pipeline runs from Pugang gas field in Dazhou, Sichuan Province, to Qingpu District of Shanghai.
Chengdu is the capital of Sichuan province in Southwest China. It is one of the three most populous cities in Western China, the other two being Chongqing and Xi'an.

input: Which former Republican won the presidential nomination at the 2012 United States Libertarian National Convention?
expected_output: Former Governor of New Mexico Gary Johnson won the presidential nomination at the 2012 United States Libertarian National Convention.
context: The 2012 United States Libertarian National Convention, in which delegates of the Libertarian Party (LP) chose the party's nominees for President of the United States and Vice President of the United States in the 2012 general election, was held May 2–6, 2012 in Las Vegas, Nevada at the Red Rock Resort Spa and Casino. Former Governor of New Mexico Gary Johnson won the presidential nomination on the first ballot.

Gary Earl Johnson (born January 1, 1953) is an American businessman, author, and politician. He was the 29th Governor of New Mexico from 1995 to 2003 as a member of the Republican Party. He was also the Libertarian Party nominee for President of the United States in the 2012 and 2016 elections.

The 2012 presidential campaign of Gary Johnson was announced on April 21, 2011. He declared his candidacy for the 2012 Republican Party nomination for President of the United States. On December 28, 2011, Johnson withdrew his candidacy for the Republican nomination, and declared his candidacy for the 2012 presidential nomination of the Libertarian Party.

The 2016 Libertarian Party presidential primaries and caucuses allowed electors to indicate non-binding preferences for the Libertarian Party's presidential candidate. The delegates nominated former New Mexico Governor Gary Johnson and former Massachusetts Governor Bill Weld at the 2016 convention.

The 2008 Libertarian National Convention was held in Denver, Colorado, where former Georgia Congressman Bob Barr won the party's presidential nomination on the sixth ballot, defeating Mary Ruwart and Wayne Allyn Root.

input: The Cinematic Orchestra was signed to the record label based in what city?
expected_output: The Cinematic Orchestra was signed to the independent record label Ninja Tune, based in London.
context: The Cinematic Orchestra is a British nu jazz and electronic music group, created in 1999 by Jason Swinscoe. The group is signed to independent record label Ninja Tune. In addition to Swinscoe, the band includes former DJ Food member PC (Patrick Carpenter) on turntables, Luke Flowers (drums), Tom Chant (saxophone), Nick Ramm (piano), Stuart McCallum (guitar) and Phil France (double bass).

Ninja Tune is an English independent record label based in London. It has satellite offices in Los Angeles and Montreal. It was founded by Matt Black and Jonathan More, better known as Coldcut and managed by Peter Quicke and others.

All Things To All Men is a song featured on the album Every Day by British nu-jazz group The Cinematic Orchestra. The song features vocals by London-born rap artist Roots Manuva and an instrumental composition from Welsh musician Rhodri Davies. It was released under the British-based independent record label Ninja Tune.

Cynthia G. Mason is a songwriter based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. She self-released albums (as cassettes) on her own label, Spiderwoman. In January 2007, she released her first nationally distributed album, "Quitter's Claim", on the High Two label, produced by guitarist Larry D. Brown, who is a member of The Cinematic Orchestra.

Domino Recording Company is a British independent record label founded in London in 1993 by Laurence Bell. It has released records by artists such as Franz Ferdinand and Arctic Monkeys, and is unrelated to the Ninja Tune roster.

input: What was the nationality of the "Lonely Hearts Killers"?
expected_output: The "Lonely Hearts Killers" were an American serial killer couple.
context: Raymond Martinez Fernandez (December 17, 1914 – March 8, 1951) and Martha Jule Beck (May 6, 1920 – March 8, 1951) were an American serial killer couple. They are believed to have killed as many as 20 women during their murderous spree between 1947 and 1949. After their arrest and trial for serial murder in 1949, they became known as "The Lonely Hearts Killers".

The Honeymoon Killers is a 1970 American crime film written and directed by Leonard Kastle, and starring Shirley Stoler and Tony Lo Bianco. It is inspired by the true story of Raymond Fernandez and Martha Beck, the notorious "lonely hearts killers" of the 1940s.
Lonely Hearts is a 2006 American film directed and written by Todd Robinson. It is based on the true story of the notorious "Lonely Hearts Killers" of the 1940s, Martha Beck and Raymond Fernandez.
Deep Crimson is a 1996 Mexican film directed by Arturo Ripstein, also based on the Fernandez-Beck murder case, though the setting and character names were changed to Mexico in the 1940s.

Sgt. Petsound's Lonely Hearts Club Band is a track-for-track mash-up of The Beach Boys' "Pet Sounds" with The Beatles' "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band" by Clayton Counts, posted on his blog under the pseudonym "The Beachles".
The Zodiac Killer was an unidentified serial killer who operated in Northern California in the late 1960s and early 1970s. The case remains one of the United States' most infamous unsolved crimes.

Fernandez and Beck were tried in New York rather than Michigan, where their first known murder occurred, because New York still had the death penalty at the time. Both were convicted and executed in the electric chair at Sing Sing Correctional Facility in March 1951.

Belle Sorenson Gunness (1859–1908?) was a Norwegian-American serial killer who lured suitors to her Indiana farm through lonely hearts advertisements in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, murdering an estimated 25 to 40 people before disappearing after a house fire.

The Manson Family was a quasi-commune that arose in California in the late 1960s, led by American criminal Charles Manson, whose members committed a series of murders in 1969 that became emblematic of the decade's darker cultural currents.

The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It was designed and built by the company of engineer Gustave Eiffel for the 1889 World's Fair and has become a global cultural icon of France.

input: What is the boiling point of water at sea level in Celsius?
expected_output: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level (standard atmospheric pressure).
context: At standard atmospheric pressure (sea level), pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, or 212 degrees Fahrenheit.
At higher altitudes, lower air pressure lowers the boiling point of water; in Denver it boils at roughly 95 degrees Celsius.
The freezing point of water at standard pressure is 0 degrees Celsius.

input: Which planet is known as the Red Planet, and why?
expected_output: Mars is known as the Red Planet because iron oxide (rust) on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.
context: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It is often called the Red Planet because iron oxide prevalent on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System and is known for its Great Red Spot, a persistent storm.
Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System because of a runaway greenhouse effect.

input: Who developed the theory of general relativity and in what year was it published?
expected_output: Albert Einstein developed the theory of general relativity, published in 1915.
context: Albert Einstein published the theory of general relativity in 1915, describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation, published in 1687, described gravity as a force between masses.
Special relativity, also by Einstein, was published in 1905 and deals with objects moving at constant speed.

input: What gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
expected_output: Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere during photosynthesis.
context: During photosynthesis, plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil, and use light energy to produce glucose and release oxygen.
Animals inhale oxygen and exhale carbon dioxide during respiration.
Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of Earth's atmosphere but most plants cannot absorb it directly from the air.

input:

The Great Barrier Reef, located off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching over 2,300 kilometres. It can be seen from outer space and is the world's biggest single structure made by living organisms. The reef is threatened by climate change, which causes mass coral bleaching events, as well as by pollution and crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks. Australia has established the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park to limit human impact, and the reef was selected as a World Heritage Site in 1981.
